plot: At 6 a.m. on Mia's birthday the bros find the cake's top layer sliding and cracked, the puppy is asleep under the table and Zeek blames Lolly's sprinkle spoon; lifting the layer back makes a leaning tower until Zeek's toothpicks hold it, and his measuring shows the crack is only on the still-warm side — warm layers slid by themselves (the warm-bottom clue) — so he apologises, angry Lolly ices over the crack and adds MIA 7 sprinkles, Mom and Dad each thank the other, Mia hugs her puppy, and she announces six friends are sleeping over tonight.

beats.say: Who cracked Mia's birthday cake? It's sliding! Somebody grab it!
Push on the other side! Hold it straight!
New episode every day. Subscribe so you don't miss what happens next.
Six in the morning. The top layer slid. A crack runs down.
The paw prints led here! The puppy wrecked the cake!
The puppy is asleep under the table. Snoring. Look.
Then who leaned that big spoon against the cake last night?
Me. It was my ladder. For the sprinkles. Our secret gift.
So your spoon pushed it over. You and your sprinkles, Lolly.
I was only trying to help. I wanted it to be perfect.
Stop. Blame later. Mom comes down at seven. We fix it now.
And keep it quiet. Seven years old only happens once.
Odd. The bottom layer is still warm. Mom baked it late.
Warm things slide. Ask any butter.
Plan one. We lift the top layer back where it belongs.
Five tiny bros lift one huge cake layer. Slowly. Very slowly.
My arms! Do I have arms? Whatever I have, it hurts!
Lift with your legs, Pim. Oh. Right. No legs either.
The layer goes back on. Then it leans. Then it leans more.
It's the leaning tower of cake! It's going again!
If it falls now, Mia's birthday starts with a ruined cake!
Hold it! Nobody move! Pim, don't sneeze!
Why would you say that? Now I need to sneeze!
Pim does not sneeze. Pim turns a darker red. Everyone waits.
Okay. It passed. Nobody say sneeze again.
Toothpicks. Bakers push toothpicks through layers to hold them.
Zeek pushes four toothpicks down through the cake. The leaning stops.
It's standing! Zeek, that actually worked!
Wait. I'm measuring. The crack is on the warm side only.
Your spoon was on the cold side, Lolly. It didn't do this.
The warm layer just slid by itself. Nobody broke it.
I blamed you for trying to help. I'm sorry, Lolly.
Apology accepted. Now hand me the icing knife. I'm angry-decorating.
Yes, chef. Right away, chef. Please don't hurt me.
Lolly spreads icing over the crack. Smooth. Fast. A little scary.
And now, the secret gift. Sprinkles. M. I. A. Seven.
Golden sprinkles land on top. Just as the stairs creak.
Places! Everybody back! We are just normal kitchen food!
Mom walks in. She stares at the sprinkles. She calls upstairs.
Mom thinks Dad decorated it. Dad thinks Mom did. Both say thanks.
That's how humans stay married. Nobody asks questions.
Should we tell them? No. Never. Absolutely not.
Then Mia runs in. The puppy wakes up under the table. Barking.
She's hugging it! She's crying happy tears! Our cake made it!
The puppy has golden sprinkles on its nose. Nobody asks why.
Best birthday in this kitchen. And nobody saw us.
Then Mia says one more thing. Six friends are sleeping over. Tonight.
Six kids? At midnight? Hungry? In OUR kitchen?
What do you think happens in the next part?
Tell me in the comments.
